best_idea: Give each attackable target a small grace area sized by its state, cut wherever two grace areas meet, commit a drag-release only onto a valid target after a real drag, and let a long press open info and suppress the click after it.
decision_why: Keep the state-sized grace with the no-overlap rule, the press and long-press split and the drag-release commit, with the dead branch removed and the pass made pure; reject the per-tile DOM grid and tile-unit px offsets.
acceptance: On a 375-wide phone a tap within 6 px outside an enemy's sprite attacks that enemy; a unit test on resolveGrace asserts two adjacent enemies' grace areas never overlap; a 380 ms hold opens the unit card and the release does not also select; a drag over at least two tiles that releases on an attackable enemy attacks it, and a release on an empty tile does nothing.
